newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-PLO summit, deal likely today - Israel.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-PLO summit, deal likely today - Israel.

text.p: Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu and the Palestinians' Yasser Arafat are likely to hold a summit on Thursday to close a deal giving Palestinians self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron, an Israeli official said.

"It's almost definite that there will be some kind of a summit this afternoon...and probably will be a final meeting in which the agreement will be initialled," Netanyahu's adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters.
"There are no outstanding issues unless the Palestinians raise a new issue or demand the reopening of an issue that has been concluded," Bar-Illan said.
In the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip, a Palestinian official who declined to be identified said a summit meeting had yet to be set and Arafat would be consulting negotiators on Thursday morning.

If initialled on Thursday, the deal could go to Israel's cabinet on Friday for approval and be signed and given Israeli parliamentary approval in time for a redeployment early next week, Bar-Illan said.

Under a 1995 Israeli-PLO peace deal, 80 percent of Hebron was due to be given self-rule nine months ago. But violence, security concerns and other issues have held up the handover. Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.
